title: The double covers of S4 are #P-hard on knots
claim: Target: let G~ be GL(2,3) or the binary octahedral group 2O, each a central extension of S4 by Z/2. For every knot K with group pi, every homomorphism pi -> S4 lifts to exactly two homomorphisms pi -> G~: the obstruction lies in H^2(pi; F2) = 0 and the lifts form a torsor for H^1(pi; F2) = Z/2. Hence the homomorphisms pi -> G~ sending meridians to lifts of transpositions (involutions in GL(2,3), elements of order 4 in 2O) number 2T(K), where T(K) counts S4 transposition colourings, and |Hom(pi, G~)| = 2 |Hom(pi, S4)|. Moreover |Hom(pi, S4)| = 4 + R(K) + 2T(K), where R(K) counts the maps sending meridians to 3-cycles (maps into A4, polynomial by BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001B) and the 4-cycle colourings number T(K) (Livingston 1995, Theorem 9). With BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A, counting homomorphisms from knot groups to S4, GL(2,3) or 2O is #P-hard, with or without the meridian condition. The closed-manifold version for GL(2,3) and 2O is not established: the identity |Hom(pi1 S3_4(K), G~)| = 8 + 2T(K) holds on some knots and fails on others, because the lifted longitude signs vary.
failure_conditions: A knot whose count of maps to G~ with meridians on lifts of transpositions differs from 2T(K), or whose unrestricted count differs from 2 |Hom(pi, S4)|.
A knot with |Hom(pi, S4)| different from 4 + R + 2T.
A failure of the group facts: G~ has centre Z/2 with quotient S4; the lifts of transpositions are involutions in GL(2,3) and elements of order 4 in 2O.
foundation_claim_scope: Knot groups given by diagrams (compact 3-manifolds with torus boundary, first homology Z); Turing reductions through BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A. Cited: Livingston 1995 Theorem 9 (proved again in CLOSED-H1-20261025-001B), asphericity of knot exteriors. Closed manifolds with bounded first homology are not covered for GL(2,3) and 2O. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof (cited: asphericity of knot exteriors, Livingston 1995 Theorem 9 as re-proved in CLOSED-H1-20261025-001B, and BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A/B); check.py (standard library, about 2 s) builds GL(2,3) and the binary octahedral group in SL(2,9), verifies their projections onto S4 with kernel the centre and the orders of transposition lifts, and on nine knots verifies by brute force |Hom(pi, G~)| = 2|Hom(pi, S4)|, 2T maps on transposition lifts, and |Hom(pi, S4)| = 4 + R + 2T; records that closed manifolds obstruct lifts and that the naive closed identity 8 + 2T fails on some knots. No human or external review
